newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico oil-tied Brady estimates revised downward.
newsitem.headline: Mexico oil-tied Brady estimates revised downward.

text.p: The value recovery rights (VRR) on Mexican Par and Discount Brady bonds will be in the money throughout 1997, but their value has been revised downwards due to falling crude oil export prices in March, Bear, Stearns said in a report released on Tuesday.
"We still expect that the VRRs will be well in the money throughout 1997," Bear, Stearns sovereign analyst Felipe Illanes said.

"Further declines in international crude prices and higher than expected U.S. inflation -- affecting the June U.S. GNP deflator-based resetting of the strike price -- could ... potentially reduce the last two payments of the year," he said.
Bear, Stearns is estimating that the June payment will come in at around $1,812 per million face of Par bonds, while that of September will reach $1,319. The December payment is seen at $855.
The Discounts are seen paying $2,788 per million face value in June, $2,030 in September and $1,315 in December.
